result.summary: The round makes no code change. Its commit message names the cause: the failing test is test_planner_runs.RunGuards.test_run_claims_before_launch_so_concurrent_callers_launch_once, which timed out on a 2 s wait under gate load, in a file T-1708 never touches. That meets the 'cause is named' criterion. I did not run the suite, so the 'tests.test_daemon and tests.test_merge pass' criterion rests on the commit message's claim of 271 passing tests. The T-1708 diff in the lineage is coherent. `_fix_parent` walks hand-filed chains with a seen-set to prevent cycles and requires the named task to be an unmerged execute task in the same goal. `stamp`, `_hold_stale_high` and `gate` no longer re-hold a task whose chain already merged. Both new tests assert the intended behaviour, including the negative case where a stray fix round for a task in a different goal leaves that task held.

comments.issue: The title regex `^fix round\b.*?\bfor held (T-\d+)` matches the task title, which comes from a Planner-filed bus task and is untrusted data. The same-goal, execute-role and unmerged checks limit the effect to marking a held task in the same goal done. A malformed title could still wrongly mark a sibling task merged. Low risk, and a human reviews merges.

The late-result guard in `gate` calls `bus.get` again after `run_gate`, but there is still a race between that check and the later hold or stamp. `stamp`'s own merged_into check narrows the window, so this is acceptable.
